Retrying failing calls

Source: vignettes/retry.Rmd
retry.Rmd
library(garnish)

Some failures are temporary: a network blip, a rate limit, a lock held by someone else. retry() calls the function again until it works or you tell it to give up. It is a port of Python’s tenacity, and is built from three questions:

  • When do we stop? (stop)
  • How long do we wait between attempts? (wait)
  • Which outcomes count as a failure? (retry)

Each has a default, so retry() on its own retries any error, immediately, forever. That is rarely what you want, so you will usually set stop.

A function that fails at first

The examples use a function that fails twice and then succeeds:

make_flaky <- function(fail_times) {
  calls <- 0
  function() {
    calls <<- calls + 1
    if (calls <= fail_times) stop("not yet (call ", calls, ")")
    paste("worked on call", calls)
  }
}

Apply retry() with %@%, or by calling it on the function:

flaky <- retry(stop = stop_after_attempt(5)) %@% make_flaky(2)
flaky()
## [1] "worked on call 3"

Deciding when to stop

stop_after_attempt(n) makes at most n attempts. When it fires, a retry_error condition is signalled:

never_works <- retry(stop = stop_after_attempt(3)) %@% make_flaky(Inf)
never_works()
## Error:
## ! Retry failed after 3 attempt(s): not yet (call 3)

The condition records what happened, so you can catch it and look:

fresh <- retry(stop = stop_after_attempt(3)) %@% make_flaky(Inf)
err <- tryCatch(fresh(), retry_error = identity)
err$attempt
## [1] 3
conditionMessage(err$error)
## [1] "not yet (call 3)"

If you would rather see the original error, set reraise = TRUE:

loud <- retry(stop = stop_after_attempt(2), reraise = TRUE) %@% make_flaky(Inf)
tryCatch(loud(), retry_error = function(e) "retry_error", error = conditionMessage)
## [1] "not yet (call 2)"

Or return a fallback instead of throwing. retry_error_callback receives the final state, a list with attempt, wait, elapsed, error and value:

safe <- retry(
  stop = stop_after_attempt(2),
  retry_error_callback = function(state) "fallback"
) %@% make_flaky(Inf)
safe()
## [1] "fallback"
Stop condition Gives up when
stop_never() never (the default)
stop_after_attempt(n) n attempts have been made
stop_after_delay(s) s seconds have passed since the first attempt
stop_before_delay(s) the next wait would pass s seconds in total
stop_any(a, b) either a or b fires
stop_all(a, b) both fire

Combine them to say “try up to 10 times, but never for more than 30 seconds”:

stop_any(stop_after_attempt(10), stop_after_delay(30))
## <garnish::stop_any>
##  @ stops:List of 2
##  .. $ : <garnish::stop_after_attempt>
##  ..  ..@ max_attempt_number: num 10
##  .. $ : <garnish::stop_after_delay>
##  ..  ..@ max_delay: num 30

Deciding how long to wait

By default retry() does not wait. For anything talking to a server you want a pause, and usually one that grows. wait_exp() doubles the wait each time:

patient <- retry(
  stop = stop_after_attempt(4),
  wait = wait_exp(multiplier = 0.01)
) %@% make_flaky(3)
system.time(res <- patient())[["elapsed"]] > 0.05
## [1] TRUE
res
## [1] "worked on call 4"

Waiting the same length of time means many clients that failed together retry together. Adding randomness spreads them out, and + combines strategies:

wait_exp(multiplier = 0.1) + wait_rand(0, 0.1)
## <garnish::wait_combine>
##  @ waits:List of 2
##  .. $ : <garnish::wait_exp>
##  ..  ..@ multiplier: num 0.1
##  ..  ..@ min       : num 0
##  ..  ..@ max       : num 4.61e+18
##  ..  ..@ exp_base  : num 2
##  .. $ : <garnish::wait_rand>
##  ..  ..@ min: num 0
##  ..  ..@ max: num 0.1
Wait strategy Waits
wait_none() no time (the default)
wait_fixed(s) s seconds
wait_rand(min, max) a random time between min and max
wait_exp() multiplier * exp_base^(attempt - 1), between min and max
wait_exp_jitter() exponential, with "full", "equal" or "decorrelated" jitter
wait_chain(a, b, ...) the n-th strategy for the n-th attempt
wait_combine(a, b) or a + b the sum of the strategies

Deciding what to retry

By default every error is retried. A bad password will not fix itself on the fifth attempt, so retry only what is temporary.

retry_if_error() matches condition classes:

calls <- 0
fetch <- retry(
  stop = stop_after_attempt(3),
  retry = retry_if_error("http_error")
) %@% function() {
  calls <<- calls + 1
  rlang::abort("bad request", class = "client_error")
}
try(fetch(), silent = TRUE)
calls
## [1] 1

It made one attempt, because client_error is not an http_error. retry_if_error_message() matches the text instead, either exactly or by regular expression:

retry_if_error_message(match = "timed? ?out")
## <garnish::retry_if_error_message>
##  @ message: NULL
##  @ match  : chr "timed? ?out"

A function can also fail without erroring, by returning something unusable. retry_if_result() retries when a predicate on the value is TRUE:

polls <- 0
poll <- retry(
  stop = stop_after_attempt(5),
  retry = retry_if_result(is.null)
) %@% function() {
  polls <<- polls + 1
  if (polls < 3) NULL else "ready"
}
poll()
## [1] "ready"

retry_never() turns retrying off, which is useful for switching it off from a setting without removing the decorator.

Seeing what is happening

Silent retries are hard to debug. The hooks run around each sleep:

logged <- retry(
  stop = stop_after_attempt(4),
  wait = wait_fixed(0.01),
  before_sleep = before_sleep_log(function(msg) cat(msg, "\n")),
  after_sleep = after_sleep_log(function(msg) cat(msg, "\n"))
) %@% make_flaky(2)
logged()
## Attempt 1 failed: not yet (call 1). Retrying in 0.01 seconds. 
## Slept 0.01 seconds after attempt 1. Retrying. 
## Attempt 2 failed: not yet (call 2). Retrying in 0.01 seconds. 
## Slept 0.01 seconds after attempt 2. Retrying.
## [1] "worked on call 3"

The defaults are before_sleep_none() and after_sleep_none(). The loggers take any function that accepts one string, so you can send the message to whatever logging package you use.

Putting it together 

fetch := retry(
  stop = stop_any(stop_after_attempt(5), stop_after_delay(30)),
  wait = wait_exp_jitter(base = 0.5, jitter = "full"),
  retry = retry_if_error_message(match = "timeout|503"),
  before_sleep = before_sleep_log(),
  reraise = TRUE
) %@% function(url) {
  # ...
}

Notes

  • Only retry things that are safe to repeat. Retrying a call that charges a card or sends an email can do it twice. Put the retry around the part that is safe.
  • Retrying hides failures. Use a stop condition, and a hook that logs, so a service that is down for an hour does not look like a slow one.
  • Decorators stack. In a %@% b %@% f, a is outermost. Put retry() outside a timing decorator to time all attempts, or inside it to time each one.
